purpose: Quantify why the parametric tensorlbm.propeller_cad geometry cannot represent the real DTMB 4119 blade, independently of the solver.

real_4119_section_table.source: OpenProp Examples/ExP03_Propeller4119_replica_design/Prop4119_input.m (joaoantoniocardoso/OpenProp), the standard DTMB 4119 replica-design input

parametric_cad_geometry.source: tensorlbm.propeller_cad.build_propeller_mask analytic elliptic chord x NACA4 half-thickness; only scalar parameters accepted

deficits.tip_chord_behavior: real 4119 tapers to c/D=0.002 at the tip; the CAD keeps c/D=0.291 (open elliptic tail) -> spurious tip loading
deficits.section_thickness: build_propeller_mask clamps the half-thickness to >= 2 lu (4 lu full), so at D=32 peak t/c = 0.40 and at D=48 t/c = 0.27, versus the real t0/c = 0.054 at 0.7R (5-7x too thick)
deficits.camber: the CAD uses NACA4 symmetric-thickness style shaping without the NACA a=0.8 meanline camber

conclusion: Independent of any solver error, the delivered blade area is 24% low, the peak chord is 32% low, the radial chord distribution is wrong, and the sections are 5-7x too thick. A KT/KQ match to DTMB 4119 experiment within 3% is not attainable from this geometry.
